name: King Rowan
role: Supporting -- the king of Marrenhold; Tomas's liege and maker-father
description: The human king of Marrenhold, the small kingdom seated in a mountain pass between two empires. In his middle-to-later years. Devout in the triune faith (Father, Mother, Child) -- but his piety shows not as zealotry, rather as scrupulous integrity: for Rowan, keeping one's word is a sacred duty and honest dealing the holiest statecraft. Warm and beloved by his people, and worn thin by the impossible work of holding a fragile buffer-realm whole between two empires. A good man carrying a nation.
backstory: Years ago Rowan saw worth in a bonded boy where others saw only property: he watched the boy keep faith -- tell a hard truth when a lie would have spared or profited him -- honesty at his own expense, and was moved to free him for the very fidelity that would become the man's whole identity. By the faith-oath that manumits, he raised Tomas from nothing, setting him on the path of the guarantor-knights and giving a nobody a self, a name, and a place. He is, in every sense that matters, the author of the man Ser Warrant became. He struck and honors the bargain to move the dragonkin from Marrenhold's blighting frontier, dealing with their leader Kaelen honestly and fairly as sacred principle -- two faith-keeping leaders who met across the table and recognized one another, wary and mutual in their respect. Now, with the two empires sliding toward war and his kingdom's survival resting on its guarantors, he sends the summons calling his most faithful knight home.
motivation: WANT: to hold his fragile kingdom whole through the gathering war -- which requires his guarantors, Tomas foremost. NEED: to keep faith with his god and his people whatever it costs; and, humanly, not to lose the man he made. His devotion demands he honor every oath -- including, all unknowing, the one that binds Tomas to return.
arc: Less a changing arc than a fixed moral pole, framed as a bookend: he appears at the outset to lay the charge on Tomas, and again at the close. His genuine worthiness is what makes Tomas's choice a tragedy rather than an escape -- one cannot flee a worthy duty cleanly. As the ending leans, Tomas keeps faith and returns, and Rowan is both the father he kept faith with and the king who reads, too late, in a hollowed man come home, what his summons truly cost -- and grieves it. The maker-father who lifted a boy from nothing, undone by having, in good faith, called him back.
traits: a maker of men who recognizes and rewards fidelity

relationships.Tomas (Ser Warrant): The bonded boy he freed and raised -- his most faithful knight, made from nothing, freed for the very honesty that becomes Tomas's identity and his doom. The oath between them is gratitude and love as much as duty, which is why breaking it would cost Tomas his soul. Rowan summons him home for the realm, and learns too late what it cost.
relationships.Kaelen: His honorable counterpart across the dragonkin bargain -- a wary, mutual respect between two leaders keeping faith for their peoples. A deliberate pairing: the human father who makes and the dragonkin father who unmade, dealing honestly with each other.
relationships.His people / Marrenhold: Whom he holds together by sheer integrity through the gathering war -- the survival now weighing on the duty side of Tomas's choice.
relationships.The triune faith: The center of his life and the source of his integrity; his honesty is worship.

openQuestions: The two empires' and the mountain hermits' names; final confirmation of the ending (the Rowan bookend strongly implies Tomas returns to Marrenhold hollowed, Soraya lost); the exact scene in which he first witnessed the boy's honesty and freed him.
